block.title: The Gallina backend runs through λANF, at 4.2× ocamlopt on rx.ir
block.p: Milestone M3 of lambda-anf.md. The reader and the three compilers of rocq/backend go through CertiRocq's λANF, AnfLower.v and nanofil-backend compile-allocated, and run on the arena of nanofil/anf. Natural numbers, positives, N and Z are 31-bit immediates or bigint blocks, characters their codes, and strings blocks of bytes, or slices of one past 64 bytes.

claim.p: On all 52 IR fixtures, for compile, compile-promoted and compile-allocated, the arena build prints the same assembly, stderr and exit status as the OCaml build, with the default nursery and with a 4096-word one under FUGC_SCRIBBLE=1 FUGC_VERIFY=1: 0 of 156 runs differ.

metrics.baseline: ocamlopt build of the same backend

block.p: That misses M3's target of 2× on rx.ir. Before the speed work it was 10× (2.2 s against 0.21 s). What closed most of it:

ul.li: inlining CertiRocq's closure builders and uncurry wrappers;
tables instead of a binary search for calls through closures;
a calling convention that passes the young index and the roots' top in arguments and the result, so that a call reads and writes nothing of the state;
a whole-program analysis of what closures' environments hold, which turns 2,223 of the backend's 3,039 calls through tables into direct calls.

block.p: The rest is 88% in the lowered functions themselves. The hot ones are small and called very often (term_eqb's atom case, Z_as_OT.compare, ZMap's bal and find), and each call pays the IR function's prologue (stack check, five callee-saved registers, the Fil-C frame) and each arena access a bounds check. Inlining every function of ten nodes or fewer bought only 5% while growing the IR by 37% and the frames of deep recursions, so it is not done. Compiling the lowered backend (64 MB of IR) takes 5 minutes, most of it in the validator, quadratic in a function's temporaries.
